papers.title: MGQL: An Executable, Small-Step Semantics of GQL
papers.journal: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages
papers.abstract: Research and development of graph query languages has been gaining traction with the increase in popularity of graph databases, specifically due to the flexible schema and other rich semantic offerings of the latter’s most common underlying data model: the property graph. This has culminated in the standardization of the ISO Graph Query Language (GQL) as ISO/IEC 39075 in 2024, the first international standard for property graph- based graph query languages. However, ISO/IEC 39075 codifies its semantics informally across 600+ pages of prose, making it difficult to formally reason about the standard or for a standard-faithful implementation. Existing formalizations are not adequate because they either: (1) significantly reduce the semantic complexity by omitting bag semantics, schemas, and composite queries on multiple graphs; (2) or significantly reduce the syntactic complexity by only considering isolated fragments such as pattern-matching, leaving the full query pipeline unformalized. Yet it is these semantic–syntactic features that make formalizing GQL non-trivial. We present MGQL, the first mechanized, small-step operational semantics for a substantial read-only fragment of GQL that is grounded in the ISO/IEC 39075 standard. Our formalization models multi-graph property graphs with mixed edge directionality and supports a large fraction of GQL pattern constructs: quantified paths and edges, directional and undirected matching, label expressions, pattern lists, and composite queries. The semantics is supported by a schema-aware type system that refines variable types via closed-graph schemas, tracks nullability, supports multiple composite query operators, and models quantified-path bindings with list types. We prove that our type system is sound, ensuring an end-to-end guarantee of well-formed queries yielding results that conform to their declared schemas. MGQL provides the first bridge between GQL’s informal specification and a mechanized implementation, enabling formal reasoning about correctness.

MGQL provides the first bridge between GQL’s informal specification and a mechanized implementation, enabling formal reasoning about correctness.

papers.title: Development of ultrafast and radiation-hard GAGG for the next-generation of High-Energy Physics calorimeters
papers.journal: Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A Accelerators Spectrometers Detectors and Associated Equipment
papers.abstract: The evolution of High Energy Physics (HEP) toward future collider experiments with High Luminosity (HL), such as the HL-LHC, requires the development of scintillating materials that combine high density, excellent radiation hardness and an ultrafast response. While Cerium-doped Gadolinium Aluminum Gallium Garnet (GAGG:Ce) offers a very high light yield and resilience to irradiation, its typical decay time of approximately 50–60 ns may lead to pile-up effects in high-rate environments. In this paper, we report on the development and multi-stage characterization of various accelerated GAGG compositions optimized for timing performance and grown by Crytur. By taking advantage of divalent co-doping to engineer the scintillation kinetics, we achieved an effective decay time ( τ d,eff ) down to 5.5 ns while maintaining a competitive light yield of several thousand photons per MeV. Laboratory characterization demonstrates that the time resolution under gamma-ray excitation is comparable to commercial GAGG, while the time resolution measured with 120 GeV pions reaches performance levels comparable to state-of-the-art LYSO:Ce,Ca. After a 1 MGy proton irradiation campaign the material retains most of its optical transmission. The results confirm that this ultrafast GAGG composition is a viable candidate for the next generation of HEP calorimetry and timing detectors.

papers.title: From waste to hyper-ductility: Micromechanical and techno-ecological assessment of ECC incorporating high-volume ultrafine marble powder
papers.abstract: Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC) offer exceptional ductility but suffer from high ecological and economic costs due to heavy cementitious binder requirements, while waste marble powder poses severe environmental disposal hazards. This study aims to evaluate the micromechanical, structural, and eco-economic impacts of utilizing ultrafine marble powder (UF-MP) as a partial to complete replacement for fly ash in PVA-ECC, hypothesizing that UF-MP can re-engineer the matrix toughness to enhance ductility while lowering embodied energy. To test this, ECC mixtures containing 2% PVA fibers were formulated with UF-MP substituting fly ash at 0%, 10%, 25%, 40%, and 100% by weight. Performance was rigorously assessed through flowability, compressive and four-point bending tests, fracture toughness evaluation, single-crack tension, SEM, TGA, and life-cycle sustainability of ECC mixtures. The results demonstrated that a 10% substitution (ECC-10) yielded the highest compressive (42.23 MPa) and flexural (12.16 MPa) strengths via micro-filling and nucleation effects. However, higher substitutions progressively reduced matrix toughness while exponentially increasing the complementary fiber-bridging energy. Consequently, the fully substituted ECC-100 exhibited a remarkable 71.37% increase in mid-span deflection (4.37 mm) accompanied by highly dense micro-cracking. SEM and TGA confirmed that high UF-MP volumes dilute rigid hydration products, transforming the fiber-matrix interface from a brittle chemical bond to a steady frictional slip. Furthermore, eco-efficiency analysis revealed a 27.2% reduction in embodied energy alongside lowered material costs. Ultimately, UF-MP successfully re-engineers the interfacial transition zone, trading absolute strength for high ductility, providing a framework where ECC-10 optimizes load-bearing capacity and ECC-100 maximizes sustainable, high deformability.

papers.title: Non-monotonic shrinkage behavior of a highly filled polymer-metal feedstock during injection molding and its relation to binder phase transitions
papers.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
papers.abstract: Abstract Highly filled polymer–metal feedstocks exhibit complex thermophysical behavior because of their high solid loading and multicomponent binder systems. In this study, the green-part shrinkage of a 17-4PH MIM feedstock containing approximately 92 wt% metal powder was investigated as a function of mold temperature, packing pressure and melt temperature. The feedstock exhibited a statistically significant non-monotonic response to mold temperature, with a maximum shrinkage of approximately 0.5% at 60 °C, whereas the polypropylene reference showed a monotonic trend. DSC analysis identified a lower-temperature transition with an onset at 51.4 °C, a peak at 62.9 °C and an enthalpy of 4.4 J/g. The Tait model described the overall PVT behavior with R² = 0.98 but did not reproduce the local thermophysical change observed between approximately 55 and 65 °C. The correspondence between the DSC transition and the shrinkage maximum suggests that binder phase behavior may contribute to the non-monotonic response; however, direct causality was not established. Changes in gate-freeze time, effective packing duration, viscosity, pressure transmission and particle rearrangement may also influence the measured shrinkage. The results identify the 55–60 °C mold-temperature interval as a critical processing range for dimensional control of the investigated feedstock.

papers.title: Design and optimization of mucoadhesive chitosan microspheres for oesophageal delivery of fluconazole
papers.abstract: Background Oesophageal candidiasis remains challenging to treat owing to rapid transit of conventional oral formulations through the oesophagus, resulting in inadequate local drug delivery and reduced therapeutic efficacy. To address these limitations, the present study aimed to develop fluconazole-loaded chitosan microspheres (FCZ-CMs)-based orodispersible tablets (ODTs) that rapidly disintegrate in the oral cavity while releasing mucoadhesive microspheres capable of adhering to oesophageal mucosa, enabling sustained localized drug delivery. Methods FCZ-CMs were developed by the emulsion cross-linking method using a 2 3 full factorial design to optimize particle size (PS), entrapment efficiency (EE), drug release (DR), and ex vivo oesophageal retention (ORT). Optimised FCZ-CMs (F9) were extensively characterized by Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), X-ray diffractometry (XRD), and in vitro drug release studies. Further, the ODTs developed by direct compression of F9 were evaluated for wetting time (WT), disintegration time (DT), drug content (DC), % drug release at 60 min (%DR), similarity ( f 1 /f 2 ), and stability under real-time and accelerated conditions. Results The optimised FCZ-CMs (F9) exhibited a PS (31.81 ± 1.14 μm), EE (84.12% ± 2.15%), DR (58.46% ± 1.89% at 60 min), and ORT (51.22% ± 2.11% at 30 min), demonstrating excellent suitability for localized oesophageal delivery. FTIR confirmed drug–polymer compatibility, SEM revealed spherical microspheres with a crenated surface morphology favourable for mucoadhesion, while DSC and XRD demonstrated reduced crystallinity of FCZ within the chitosan matrix. The ODTs loaded with F9 displayed high DC (99.14% ± 0.58%), short WT (19.62 ± 0.51s), and DT (23.83 ± 0.86s). The dissolution profile of ODTs remained comparable to that of F9 ( p > 0.05 ), with drug release of 53.16% ± 1.24% at 60 min and similarity factor ( f 2 = 80) and difference factor ( f 1 = 8 ), confirming that the compression process did not significantly alter the release behaviour of the optimised microspheres. The formulation also remained stable under both real-time and accelerated storage conditions. Conclusion The optimised ODTs successfully translated the performance of FCZ-CMs into a patient-friendly, oesophageal-targeted drug delivery system without compromising their controlled-release or mucoadhesive characteristics. The use of a simple, reproducible, and scalable direct compression process, together with preservation of microsphere functionality following tablet compression, highlights the translational potential of this platform for localized treatment of oesophageal candidiasis and deserves further clinical investigation.

papers.title: A recyclable g-C3N4/Biochar@Pd hybrid nanocatalyst for high-performance Suzuki, Stille and CN coupling reactions
papers.abstract: To make progress in green chemistry, it is important to use stable heterogeneous catalysts from sources that can be reused. Biochars have attracted much attention for their sustainability and environmental friendliness. However, the general application of these compounds in C C and C N cross-coupling reactions catalyzed by palladium remains to be achieved. In this study, a new nanocatalyst g-C 3 N 4 /Biochar@Pd with stability and catalytic efficiency has been prepared for the cross-coupling reactions. The catalyst was prepared by thermal polycondensation (first step) and supported on the surface of palladium (last step). Then, its properties were investigated by FT-IR, XRD, SEM, TEM, EDX, ICP-OES, BET and TGA techniques. The catalyst performance was investigated in C N, Suzuki, and Stille coupling reactions. In the C N reaction, arylamines were obtained in 83–96% yields. In the Suzuki and Stille reactions, yields of 83–98% were obtained, depending on the substrate. The reactivity order of the halides was I > Br > Cl, and electron-donating groups increased the reaction rate. The g-C 3 N 4 /Biochar@Pd nanocatalyst was reused in five consecutive cycles. This indicates that the catalyst is stable and can be effectively used in cross-coupling reactions.

papers.title: Casting Environment and Water Retention Modulate β-Sheet Crystallization and Shelf Stability of Native Bombyx mori Silk Fibroin Films
papers.abstract: Abstract The performance and shelf life of Bombyx mori silk fibroin biomaterials are governed by β-sheet crystallinity, which determines solubility, degradation, and mechanical properties. However, controlling β-sheet crystallinity during processing and storage remains a major challenge because the metastable Silk I structure can convert to the β-sheet-rich, insoluble Silk II form. Here, native silk fibroin dope extracted directly from the gland was dissolved in water and cast into films under ambient or vacuum conditions, then aged and stored under controlled environments to identify the processing variables governing β-sheet formation. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) showed that freshly cast films were amorphous and that a crystallization exotherm emerged only after prolonged aging (≥2 months) of ambient-cast films, whereas vacuum-cast films were more resistant to crystallization across concentrations and storage conditions. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed that ambient-cast films retained more loosely bound water than vacuum-cast films, while tightly bound water remained comparable, implicating loosely bound water as the plasticizer that enables molecular rearrangement. Quantitative magic angle spinning (MAS) solid-state NMR of 13C-Ala-labeled films confirmed that fresh and aged films remained predominantly amorphous (10–24% Ala β-sheet), demonstrating that the DSC exotherm arises from thermally induced crystallization of a water-plasticized precursor rather than from a pre-existing β-sheet order. Upon thermal annealing, fresh ambient-cast films reached 75% Ala β-sheet compared with only 38% for vacuum-cast films, demonstrating that the casting environment establishes the upper limit of β-sheet conversion. These findings provide a practical processing strategy for tailoring crystallinity and shelf stability: ambient casting promotes subsequent crystallization, vacuum casting preserves a low-crystallinity amorphous state, and dry storage minimizes β-sheet crystallization.
papers.summary: Abstract The performance and shelf life of Bombyx mori silk fibroin biomaterials are governed by β-sheet crystallinity, which determines solubility, degradation, and mechanical properties. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed that ambient-cast films retained more loosely bound water than vacuum-cast films, while tightly bound water remained comparable, implicating loosely bound water as the plasticizer that enables molecular rearrangement. These findings provide a practical processing strategy for tailoring crystallinity and shelf stability: ambient casting promotes subsequent crystallization, vacuum casting preserves a low-crystallinity amorphous state, and dry storage minimizes β-sheet crystallization.

papers.title: Microfibrillation Processing as an Industry‐Relevant Strategy for Upcycling Mixed Post‐Consumer Polyolefin Waste
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Post‐consumer polyolefin waste streams frequently contain immiscible polyethylene (PE) and polypropylene (PP) mixtures that exhibit poor interfacial adhesion and limited mechanical performance, restricting their recycling potential. In this work, microfibrillation processing was investigated as a low‐cost strategy to upgrade recycled PE/PP blends without relying on extensive compatibilization. Blends containing 75 wt.% PE and 25 wt.% PP were processed as conventional non‐drawn systems and as microfibrillar composites (MFCs), with and without commercial compatibilizers. The effects of morphology development on the thermal, mechanical, and fracture behavior of the materials were systematically evaluated. Scanning electron microscope observations confirmed the in situ transformation of the dispersed PP phase into elongated microfibrils after drawing, while differential scanning calorimetry and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy analyses indicated that neither microfibrillation nor compatibilizer addition significantly altered the crystallinity or chemical structure of the blends. Microfibrillated systems exhibited higher stiffness than the corresponding non‐drawn blends, together with a remarkable increase in fracture toughness, reaching improvements of up to 125%. Compatibilizers promoted fibril refinement and improved interfacial interactions; however, their influence on the final mechanical performance of the MFCs was limited. The results demonstrate that morphology control through microfibrillation is an effective approach for enhancing the performance of recycled immiscible PE/PP blends, providing a simple and economically attractive route for the high‐value reutilization of mixed polyolefin waste streams within a circular economy framework.

papers.title: PLA/PCL/SiO2 Composite Printing Plates: Towards More Sustainable Embellishment Printing Applications
papers.abstract: Replacing conventional petroleum-based materials in printing technology with sustainable alternatives is an approach to reducing the environmental impact of printing processes. In this research, biodegradable printing plates based on polylactic acid (PLA), polycaprolactone (PCL), and silicon dioxide (SiO2) nanoparticles were produced for embellishment printing applications, including relief printing and foil stamping. Structural properties were examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), while thermal behaviour was characterized using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). Mechanical properties were defined through tensile testing, hardness, and surface roughness measurements. Printing plates were produced by laser engraving, and relief geometry was measured to evaluate printing plate feasibility. The plates were exposed to 80, 100, and 120 °C for 5, 10, and 15 min, followed by evaluation of mechanical properties, surface features, and relief stability. Initial functional assessment was conducted through printing trials to obtain embossed reliefs and foil-transferred prints. The results showed that SiO2 nanoparticles increased thermal stability and stiffness and reduced thermally induced variations in hardness and thickness. SiO2-containing plates exhibited engraved line dimensions closer to nominal values. All produced plates presented well-defined embossed elements, while successful foil transfer was achieved with PLA/PCL/SiO2 70/30/3, 80/20/3, and 90/10/3 formulations. The 80/20/3 and 90/10/3 blends showed the best foil stamping performance.

papers.title: Bioactive chitosan dressings functionalized with indole alkaloids suppress biofilm development and virulence traits in bacterial species relevant to wound infections
papers.abstract: Abstract Aims Chronic wound infections are frequently associated with biofilm-forming pathogens that impair healing and reduce the effectiveness of antimicrobial therapies. This study evaluated the antimicrobial, antibiofilm, synergistic, and antivirulence activities of two indole alkaloids, 3-(1H-indol-3-yl)propanoic acid (C1) and 1H-indole-2-carboxylic acid (C2), and investigated their incorporation into chitosan-based biodressings for infected wound management. Methods and Results Antimicrobial activity was evaluated by agar diffusion, minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC), biofilm inhibition, and checkerboard assays. Cytotoxicity was assessed using RAW 264.7 macrophages and HaCaT keratinocytes. Biodressings were characterized by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis, porosity, and release kinetics, while antimicrobial activity and gene expression were evaluated by agar diffusion and RT-qPCR. Both compounds exhibited broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, particularly against Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis, inhibited biofilm formation at sub-MIC concentrations, and showed synergistic or additive interactions with conventional antibiotics. The alkaloids displayed low cytotoxicity and were successfully incorporated into chitosan matrices, showing a biphasic release profile over the evaluated period while preserving antimicrobial activity. Functionalized biodressings significantly downregulated genes involved in adhesion (fimH), biofilm formation (icaA, icaD, aap, and pslA), quorum sensing (lasR), and virulence regulation (sarA). Conclusions Indole alkaloid-loaded chitosan biodressings constitute a promising multifunctional platform that combines antibacterial, antibiofilm, antibiotic-potentiating, and antivirulence activities while maintaining favorable cytocompatibility. These findings support further investigation of indole alkaloid-loaded chitosan biodressings as a potential biomaterial-based strategy for managing wound-associated bacterial infections.

papers.title: Functionalizing silicone towards skin-compatible shape-memory actuators and sphincter-inspired valves
papers.abstract: Abstract Soft robotic systems are increasingly deployed in applications that demand safe, compliant, and intimate interaction with the human body, including wearables, biomedical devices, and ingestible robots. While silicone elastomers are a foundational material for such systems due to their elasticity, robustness, and thermal stability, existing silicone-based shape memory polymer (SMP) composites generally rely on non-biocompatible fillers or require extreme, clinically impractical conditions. This limits their use in scenarios that require tissue-compatible actuation and fluidic control near or on the body surface. Herein, we introduce a class of shape-memory silicone composites incorporating phase-change paraffin wax as a skin-compatible stiffness-modulating filler and ultra-thin nickel (Ni) wires as integrated Joule-heating elements. In these composites, silicone provides an elastic matrix while dispersed paraffin wax globules enable thermally programmable shape fixation and recovery. The composites retain the characteristic thermal and chemical features of their paraffin and silicone constituents, with differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) identifying paraffin-related transitions at approximately 51 – 56 °C, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) confirming the combined thermal stability of the composite constituents, and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy indicating a physically blended composite. The resulting materials achieve both linear and non-linear actuation modes, together with thermally modulated stiffness. Building on these capabilities, we realize a proof-of-concept sphincter-inspired soft valve capable of modulating fluid flow, illustrating their possible application for fluidics regulation in soft robotic and wearable systems. These results demonstrate the potential of the paraffin-filled shape-memory silicone composites for skin-compatible and surface-interfacing soft robotic systems.
